Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-07-17 | AAPL | Hold | -0.2% | +0.4% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at $333.74 with a constructive bias: keep the core at standard/target weight, put no new money to work at the current price, and pre-commit triggers for the next add rather than chasing into the 334.68–335.00 ceiling ahead of the late-July Q3 FY2026 print. If already overweight or concentrated into earnings, trim back to target into this strength and consider a modest protective collar/put spread; if flat or underweight, do not chase — stage adds at a confirmed breakout close above ~335 on >60M shares (small tranche, fast failed-breakout exit back below 335) or on a controlled pullback into $319–322 (10 EMA) that holds support, sized at half the intended add and ~45% smaller than an equivalent May-regime allocation given ATR 8.13. Trail risk under the 10 EMA ($319.73) on a closing basis with $308.63 as the hard thesis invalidation.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull owns direction and the bear owns entry, and both legs are unrebutted — that two-sided balance, plus the convergence of all three analysts on HOLD, is why the answer is Hold-and-prepare rather than either a chase or a trim.

The bull case is not contested and should not be faded: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew +16.6% YoY, gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 47.0%, operating margin is 32.3%, EPS +21.8%, with ~$62B net cash and ~$78.3B of H1 free cash flow. The technical structure is a fully ordered, rising stack — $333.74 above the 10 EMA ($319.73), 50 SMA ($302.65) and 200 SMA ($274.22) — with a genuinely young momentum thrust: MACD crossed zero on July 6 and has climbed 5.24 → 7.87 → 8.82, the histogram bottomed at −2.79 on June 25 and is now +3.34 and expanding, and the breakout came on confirming volume. The aggressive analyst's core point is correct: an eleven-session thrust with a rising 50-day and accelerating earnings is not a topping pattern to fade, and the several prior AAPL Underweight/stand-aside calls that misread an inside-one-ATR level as a rejection (costing ~+7–8% of alpha) are a real warning against defaulting to caution here. The China Apple Intelligence approval is a genuine, durable positive against Huawei/Xiaomi in the largest smartphone market.

The bear wins the narrower and decisive fight — the entry. At $333.74 AAPL is extended: RSI 71.65, MFI ~0.895, +10.3% above the 50 SMA, +7.6% above the VWMA ($310.27), pressed directly into the 334.68–335.00 resistance shelf, with ATR widened to 8.13 and a binary Q3 FY2026 print late this month. The conservative analyst's asymmetry math is fair for fresh money — roughly 7.5% downside to the 308.63 invalidation versus ~1.6% to the 339.20 upper band — which is exactly the risk the neutral analyst correctly caps by requiring support to hold and momentum not to deteriorate before any add. Critically, even the aggressive "loaded spring" argument is a case for buying pullbacks/breakouts, not for adding at $333.74; there is no voice in the room arguing to buy at the current tick. The bull also treated the reacceleration as removing event risk, which it does not: buybacks are down ~25% YoY (~$37.0B), R&D is +33.6%, intangibles jumped ~$12.5B in six months (likely an unquantified acquisition), the effective tax rate is 17.5% vs ~15%, and H1 operating cash flow was flattered by ~$11B of lower cash taxes — so the operating-leverage story is real but not a free pass into the print. On catalysts, the China approval lacks quantified rollout timing, monetization, or approved scope (news sample only 20 of 160 records, all from the final day); CXMT is a congressional letter to Commerce, not an enacted rule, but it is a live supply-chain headline risk; TSMC's $100B U.S. build and Buffett's CEO-transition endorsement are sentiment/direction, not governance solutions.

On balance, Underweight/Sell is unsupportable against a reaccelerating, net-cash franchise in a rising stack, and Overweight would signal adding at an extended price directly into resistance before a binary event — the worse entry than the 2026-07-10 setup that still worked (+7.4% five-day alpha). So Hold at target weight, constructive and pre-committed, is the correct expression. Applying the 2026-07-10 lesson that a trigger within ~0.5% of price is more likely a break than a rejection: the >335 breakout is only ~0.4% away, so it should be pre-committed as a small tranche with a fast failed-breakout exit rather than passively watched.

What would change the call: upgrade to Overweight if Q3 FY2026 confirms mid-teens revenue growth with gross margin near 48–49% and AAPL either holds a controlled pullback into $319–322 or clears $335 on >60M shares that holds on retest — then scale in half-size first. Downgrade to Underweight on a Q3 print with revenue growth below ~10% or gross margin materially below 48%, evidence of memory-cost margin compression or App Store deceleration, or a close below $308.63 on expanding volume. Explicitly missing and not papered over: any valuation multiple (P/E, EV/FCF, forward estimates), consensus/estimate revisions, options/IV pricing for the hedge, and the caller's actual AAPL weight, cost basis and cash.

**Price Target**: 345.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months tactical (spanning the late-July Q3 FY2026 print); 12-24 months structural

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window is too short to judge a 3-6 month Hold thesis: raw -0.2% with +0.4% alpha vs SPY is flat noise, consistent with a price pinned below the 334.68–335.00 shelf rather than a verdict on the directional call. It mildly supports the entry-discipline leg — not chasing at $333.74 cost nothing and the extended RSI/ATR setup has not yet resolved — while leaving the bull case (growth, margins, rising stack) and the >335 breakout trigger untested. The lesson: when a Hold hinges on a pre-committed trigger only ~0.4% away, note at the outset that a 5-day flat tape is uninformative and that judgment waits on the Q3 print, rather than treating the window as evidence either way.

[2026-07-16 | AAPL | Overweight | -3.5% | -1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — own the reacceleration and the fresh China AI catalyst, but stage the entry and cap pre-Q3 size instead of chasing the $333 record print. Because holdings/cash are unknown, express sizing against a standard single-name weight: build toward ~1.0x before the late-July Q3 print, then scale only to ~1.2–1.4x after the print confirms the catalyst is converting to demand. Deploy ~25–30% of the intended position only on stabilization above $316 (never on first touch, and not between $320–$334), add another ~25–30% into the $301–$316 confluence on a reclaim/volume signal rather than a falling knife, and keep ~30–40% dry powder for a volume-confirmed close above $335 or post-earnings confirmation. If the caller is already above standard weight, trim into $333–$335 and hold a core; size the starter so a gap through the $299 stop stays inside the risk budget, treat a close below the 50-SMA ($301.66) on expanding volume as a pause on adds, and the 200-SMA (~$274) as thesis invalidation.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is decided by the fundamentals, structure, and catalyst; the size is decided by entry timing and event risk — and that split lands on a disciplined Overweight. The aggressive analyst carried the substantive cases and neither opponent contested them: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.2B (+16.6%), EPS $2.01 (+21.8%), gross margin 49.3% (+230bps), H1 operating cash flow $82.6B (+53%), FCF ~$78.3B, net cash ~$61.9B with debt-to-equity falling from 1.34 to ~0.80. The trend stack is fully aligned (333.26 > 10-EMA 316.62 > 50-SMA 301.66 > rising 200-SMA 273.82; MACD 7.87 vs 4.64 signal; price above VWMA 300.72), and the China Apple Intelligence approval via Alibaba's Qwen with Baidu is a dated, regulator-cleared event that closes a specific feature-parity gap, corroborated across multiple sources. That combination rules out Underweight/Sell and rules out standing aside.

What kept this from being a full-size chase is the conservative/neutral case, which the aggressive analyst never fully answered. Entry is genuinely extended: RSI 71.43, price ~5.3% above the 10-EMA and ~10.5% above the 50-SMA, pinned at the $334.79 upper Bollinger band, ATR 8.30 (~2.5% daily) after a -12.7% three-week drawdown in late June; the $299 stop is defensible normal-day math but not gap-proof into the late-July Q3 print, which the conservative correctly frames as a binary event (IDC itself flagged China demand "pulled ahead"). The quality caveats are real and unrefuted: the +53% OCF vs +17% net income gap includes working-capital timing, R&D is up ~33.6% YoY and the tax rate is rising, ~$12.5B of intangibles moved with unclear origin, partner/concession economics on the China deals are undisclosed (permission is not yet proven demand), the 261.8M-share June flush distorts VWMA precision, and Jefferies "prefers Amazon" is a relative-preference call rather than negative evidence on Apple's figures.

Deciding between the two sizing camps: the aggressive analyst's 1.2–1.4x before a binary print is above-normal exposure to a single name at record highs with elevated ATR — too loose. The conservative analyst's 0.5–0.75x cap with post-earnings-only participation is too tight and, per our own recent AAPL reflections, has repeatedly cost 5-day alpha by letting entry mechanics quietly become underweighting (the +5.4%/+4.5%/+1.8% windows where the dip never arrived and only the starter participated). The neutral framework wins on the merits: keep the full bullish thesis, but stage capital, hold pre-Q3 at or below ~1.0x standard, buy the $316/$301–$316 confluence only on confirmation, keep dry powder for a volume-confirmed breakout above $335 or a post-Q3 report, and scale toward 1.2–1.4x only once earnings and volatility give evidence the catalyst is converting to demand.

What would change the call: a decisive close below $301.66 on expanding volume with MACD rolling negative pauses adds and moves toward Underweight; a break of the 200-SMA (~$274) invalidates the thesis and warrants exiting toward flat; Q3 gross margin rolling over from 49.3% on memory pass-through, China discount-driven share defense, or disclosure that the China/Alibaba/Baidu economics are poor — any of these shifts to Underweight. Conversely, confirmed China sell-through/upgrade data, Services reacceleration, GM holding near 49%, or resolution of the ~$12.5B intangibles and partner economics upgrades to Buy and the full 1.2–1.4x overweight. Explicit data gaps, flagged not papered over: no valuation multiples, no consensus/estimate revisions, no insider-transaction data, no China sell-through confirmation, and no disclosed partner economics — informational holes that argue for staged entry, not for avoiding the position.

**Price Target**: 345.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-underwritten at the late-July Q3 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -1.8% is mild and the window is too short to judge a 3-6 month staged-entry thesis, but it does not validate the call either. The loss undercuts the timing premise that $320–$334 should be avoided while stabilization above $316 could be bought, since price moved against the entry zone immediately rather than extending. Next time, set the first tranche deeper at the $301–$316 confluence unless volume confirms a reclaim, and pre-commit to a starter size that keeps a 5-day adverse move from costing more than a fraction of the risk budget.

[2026-07-15 | AAPL | Hold | -0.5% | +0.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at benchmark weight. Do not add at $327.50: with only ~0.7% of room to the upper Bollinger Band ($329.83) against an ATR of $8.33 (~2.5% of price), new capital is poorly compensated, and all three risk analysts, the trader, and the research plan converge on that. Keep the core position for the reported fundamentals and stacked uptrend, stage a ~25–30% add-on reserve only on confirmed pullbacks ($313 then ~$301) or a genuine post-event breakout, and hedge ~50% of delta (or trim 10–15% into strength above $327.50) through the imminent Q3 print. Cap total exposure near benchmark to ~110–125% of standard until Q3 and the $12.5B intangibles question clear. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate splits across time horizons and, on the only actionable question — what to do with capital today — converges to Hold. The bull owns direction: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.2B (+16.6% YoY), gross margin 49.3% (+220 bps), operating margin 32.3%, EPS $2.01 (+21.8%), ~$78.3B H1 FCF, ~$53.6B net cash, plus a technically stacked structure (price $327.50 > 10 EMA $312.92 > 50 SMA $300.53 > 200 SMA $273.43, MACD 6.60 vs 3.84 signal with expanding histogram, price above VWMA $296.42). The bear conceded none of that is broken, so the core stays — the $327.50 close the session after a KeyBanc Underweight reads as demand absorbing bad news, not distribution.

But the bear and neutral analysts win the entry, and that governs new capital. At $327.50 there is only ~0.7% upside to resistance ($329.83) against a $8.33 ATR, with RSI 68.77, +19% in three weeks, 9% above the 50 SMA and ~20% above the 200 SMA. The aggressive $296 stop is ~9.6% away (nearly four ATRs) — a wide swing stop that ignores gap risk into a binary Q3 print. The quality-of-earnings jabs survive: +53% H1 OCF flattered by working-capital swings and cash taxes of $20.4B vs $31.7B; a +$12.5B net intangibles jump alongside a 25% buyback cut ($37.0B) leaving organic-vs-acquired growth unresolved; R&D +33.6% and a tax rate of 17.5% vs 15.5% creating a plausible deceleration of EPS toward low-to-mid teens; and unrebutted KeyBanc forward worries (weaker hardware demand, slower Services, price-hike elasticity). No KeyBanc target, Q3 guidance, consensus, or 10-Q intangible footnote exists in the dataset — that absence is why the reserve must not be pre-committed.

I adopt the neutral analyst's framework over both extremes: the aggressive pre-committed breakout chase at the upper band (and 125% sizing) right before Q3 is uneconomic, while the conservative cap-at-benchmark-forever is too rigid for a name still expanding margins on a stacked uptrend. Hold is the disciplined synthesis — full exposure to a confirmed trend, no chase into resistance and a binary event, and a smaller, confirmation-gated reserve. Upgrades to Overweight on a decisive close above $329.83 on ≥70M volume with follow-through, ideally post-Q3 with Services reaccelerating and hardware holding at ~49% gross margin. Downgrades toward Underweight on a decisive break of the $296.42 VWMA on expanding volume, a combined Q3 Services/hardware miss with margin compression, or confirmation that much of the growth was acquired rather than organic; $273.43 (200 SMA) is structural invalidation.

**Price Target**: 340.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months (spanning the imminent Q3 print)

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +0.5% (raw -0.5%) is consistent with a Hold but far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis built around the Q3 print and $340 target. The window modestly supports the entry caution — price stalled below the $329.83 upper band rather than breaking out, so declining to add at $327.50 cost nothing and the hedge/trim-into-strength advice looks early-right rather than wrong. Lesson: when upside to resistance (~0.7%) is under a third of ATR, treat the "no-add" call as a volatility trade, not a directional one, and judge it on whether the band actually caps price over the following 10–15 sessions, not 5.

[2026-07-14 | AAPL | Overweight | +4.1% | +4.6% | 5d]

**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Own AAPL but earn the overweight in stages rather than taking the full increment at $314.86 into event risk. Build to roughly 1.05-1.10x a standard allocation pre-event: Tranche 1 of the incremental overweight near the 10-EMA ($309.68-$310) on stabilization, Tranche 2 into the $299.58-$300.40 50-SMA/mid-band confluence if it holds, and reserve the final ~0.10x plus any breakout tranche for a decisive close above $325.61 on rising volume, ideally after the late-July Q3/TSMC prints. **Investment Thesis**: The bull wins the question of whether AAPL is worth owning; the bear wins only the question of how much to pay today — hence a staged Overweight, not a Buy and not a Hold. Substance is decisive: H1 FY2026 revenue +16.1% to $254.94B (Q2 +16.6%), diluted EPS +21.8%, gross margin 48.6%/Q2 49.3%, operating margin 34.0%, ~$78.3B H1 free cash flow (~30.7% margin), ~$61.9B net cash, and record 20% global smartphone share while global Q2 shipments fell 11% — taking share and expanding margins in a shrinking market. **Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: not provided

What this window supports is the thesis's own admission that entry-price caution has repeatedly cost AAPL alpha — price ran rather than pulling back to the 10-EMA or 50-SMA, so Tranche 2 and the breakout tranche above $325.61 likely went unfilled and the staged build captured only part of the move. Lesson for next time: when the trend is fully stacked (rising 10/50/200-SMA, expanding MACD histogram, RSI mid-range), pre-commit a larger first tranche on strength and stop treating the pullback as the base case.
